chapter: Chicago and New York with Dizzy Gillespie
title: Losing the Cubana Be score in a taxi
summary: He left the score of Cubana Be, Cubana Bop in a taxi, and Gil Fuller rebuilt it from the recording.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Gil Fuller was involved with you guys a little bit also?
He got involved after I had lost the score to Cubana Be, Cubana Bop.
I lost the score. I left the score in a taxicab.
I’ll tell you that he did a wonderful job. I know of no-one else who could do that.
You lost the score in a taxicab?
I left it in a taxi.
So you talked to Gil about what was in the score, because you had done it. And then what? You guys started putting it back together, re-creating it?

I think he had the recording, and from the recording he made – from the recording of the Carnegie Hall thing, the guys had the music. They already had the music. It’s just the score that got lost. He had time. He had a lot of time then to listen.
